brief: GS's Duttenhoefer's Daily (28 Sep 2026) recaps a session where the S&P rose 51bps to 7743 (+13% ytd) on tech strength even as market breadth stayed extremely low, GS's sentiment indicator sat firmly negative, and breadth hit its lowest since 2000, while the Nasdaq 100 made new highs on a 7-of-8-day streak. The 10-year yield's seventh straight monthly rise (longest in 50 years) revives a short case on Non-Profitable Tech: despite the rates correlation recently breaking on higher retail participation and solid nominal growth, GS still sees a compelling setup to short given 100bp+ of yield rise and 20%+ one-year outperformance versus the S&P. Separately, GS estimates AI users would need to spend roughly $1 trillion annually on AI applications for hyperscalers to earn adequate returns, against $1.5 trillion in 2026 global software spend and $1.8 trillion in potential US labor-productivity gains; hyperscaler cloud revenue growth accelerated from 25% to 48% year over year. The Trump/Xi summit extended the trade truce to January 2027 with a tariff-cut recommendation body and a November AI dialogue. GS expects Micron's Sep 30 earnings to beat consensus and guidance on tight supply/demand, and raised its estimates.
